verdict.rationale: The evidence shows a scaling path. Svelte can be built standalone, with `npm run build` emitting plain HTML/JS/CSS to `dist`. SvelteKit then covers full applications, with routing, server rendering and mixed rendering modes per page. Nothing documents embedding or mounting Svelte into just a portion of an existing page, so the 'small part of a page' end of the story is only implied. missing for 10: documented mounting of a component into part of an existing non-Svelte page, explicit incremental-adoption/migration guidance, independent hands-on corroboration of partial-page adoption

support.subject: As a developer, I can incrementally adopt the framework, scaling from a small part of a page up to a full application

citations.quote: With this, `npm run build` will generate HTML, JS, and CSS files inside the `dist` directory.
If you're coming from React, SvelteKit is similar to Next. If you're coming from Vue, SvelteKit is similar to Nuxt.
SvelteKit allows for nicely mixing and matching different rendering types on different pages.
You create pages by adding files to the `src/routes` directory of your project.
